content: API reference demo This is a live API reference , generated by clean-jsdoc-theme — the exact output you get from pointing JSDoc at the theme. Every page here was built from one small, fully-commented sample module in src/; nothing was written by hand. Press Ctrl K to fuzzy-search every symbol, or browse from the sidebar. Toggle light/dark in the header, and use the copy page button at the top of any page to hand its Markdown to Claude, ChatGPT, or Perplexity. Start exploring - sample-api — the module page. It opens with an [!INFO] callout, a walkthrough, and install — all authored inline in the @module doc comment. - Cache — a documented class: constructor, properties, and methods, each rendered as its own section with parameters, return types, and @example blocks. - createCache — a factory function, showing {@link} cross-references resolved to real anchors. What it shows off - Server-rendered pages with lazy-hydrated islands — fast, and usable with no JS. - A companion .md beside every page (what the copy-page button serves to LLMs). - Source: file:line links into a read-only Monaco viewer on the source pages. - The theme's authoring components — callouts, steps, and tabs — written straight into JSDoc comments, not just prose. New here? The clean-jsdoc-theme Guide link in the sidebar opens the full documentation — installation, configuration, and theming.

description: A small, fully-documented sample module that exists purely to demonstrate what an API reference page looks like when generated by clean-jsdoc-theme . It is not a real library — it is a showcase of the common JSDoc constructs (classes, methods, params, returns, examples, typedefs, and cross-references) and the theme's authoring components, all written directly in this doc comment. [!INFO] Everything below — this callout, the stepper, and the tabs — is authored inline in the @module doc comment. The same [!NOTE] / [!TIP] / [!WARNING] / [!CAUTION] markers work too. Quick start Create a {@link Cache}, optionally capping how many entries it holds: const cache = new Cache({ maxSize: 2 }); set() returns the cache, so calls chain: cache.set('a', 1).set('b', 2); get() returns the value and marks the entry as recently used: cache.get('a'); // => 1 Install it with your package manager of choice: npm install --save-dev jsdoc clean-jsdoc-theme pnpm add -D jsdoc clean-jsdoc-theme

Returns - boolean — true if the key is cached. void" / Remove every entry from the cache. Returns - void Instance Fields The maximum number of entries this cache will hold.
